react_result.final_narrative_text: The differential metabolite set converges overwhelmingly on KEGG:hsa00350 'Tyrosine metabolism' across three independent paradigms — RaMP multi-DB ORA (FDR = 1.39e-09), Mummichog m/z-network ranking (p = 0.00168, top MUMM hit), and MetaboAnalystR KEGG PSEA (p = 6.058e-06, rank 1). In parallel, SMPDB disease-curated pathways for Alkaptonuria (SMPDB:SMP00169), Tyrosinemia Type I (SMPDB:SMP00218), and Dopamine β-hydroxylase deficiency (SMPDB:SMP00498) all achieve the same extreme FDR (1.12e-09), sharing exactly the same four driver metabolites: L-tyrosine, norepinephrine, fumaric acid, and 3,4-dihydroxyphenylacetaldehyde. The biological picture is one of systemic perturbation of tyrosine catabolism, spanning the canonical L-DOPA → dopamine → norepinephrine catecholamine arm and the homogentisate → fumarylacetoacetate → fumarate arm that feeds the TCA cycle. 5,6-Dihydroxyindole, a melanin-pigment precursor, and homogentisic acid, the diagnostic metabolite of alkaptonuria, further implicate the downstream aromatic branching of this pathway. The secondary hit on lysine metabolism via L-allysine and L-lysine reflects elastin/collagen crosslinking disruption, a known extra-skeletal manifestation of altered tyrosine flux. The treatment group therefore shows a coordinated dysregulation of aromatic amino acid catabolism with simultaneous catecholamine, melanin-pigment, and connective-tissue axes affected.
